name: Uma Ibrahim

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does a working day look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I play the simpler cello line for a town string trio, make practice tracks and help the lead cellist with beginners. I finished secondary school and began paid music six years ago after running a stationery counter. At 58 I still mark fingerings in pencil; I like the quiet moment before a pupil finds the note.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does that work fit with home life?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner repairs bicycles and our children are grown. We own our flat, have nine months of expenses saved and my booked wedding sets pay better than most junior music work. There are plenty of groups nearby, though an advert is not a booked fee. I use AI daily to sort rehearsal dates, then check against the signed hall diary.

say: I'd welcome **tidier date lists** with each player's fee written down.
I'd say the **first note** still comes from a bow.
think: Our **nine-month reserve** and partner wage cover a moved wedding.
My **paid sets** should continue in this mild scenario.
do: Confirm **six paid weddings** and two assisted pupils this week.
Save **one-quarter of extra fees** after flat charges and cello repairs while checking dates against the signed diary.
feel: I feel **calm** while paid sets and household income are secure.
S0.quote: The first note still has to come from a bow.
fieldNote: Her **higher junior pay** comes from six booked weddings, with nine months of household expenses already saved.
Daily **AI date sorting** is existing use, checked against the signed diary.

steps.text: Keep six paid weddings and two assisted pupils; check dates against signed diary
Save one-quarter of extra cleared wedding fees after flat charges and cello repairs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the trio that tidier date lists are welcome if each player's fee remains on the sheet. The first note still has to come from a bow.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our nine-month reserve and my partner's workshop wage give us room for a moved wedding. I do not expect this mild AI change to take my paid sets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll confirm the next six paid weddings and my two assisted pupils. In the first year of this small change I'll keep checking AI date lists against the signed diary and save a quarter of each extra paid wedding fee after flat charges and cello repairs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the bookings we have. A shifted date would be annoying, but it would not empty the food account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened when a wedding moved?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A couple moved their reception last summer and the trio lost the Saturday. The manager paid a cancellation fee because it was written into our contract.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do you check a date list?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I check the hall number and the three musicians' arrival times on paper. Last month a date list put us at the wrong entrance.

say: I'd ask the trio manager which **practice-track orders** the new software would replace first.
I'd seek **written live fees** before holding weekends.
think: Tracks provide **one fifth** of my own music pay from recordings.
Our **nine-month reserve** cannot replace recurring orders.
do: Compare **ten track invoices** and request three months of paid trio dates.
Learn **AI part checking** after a paid lead lesson on owned nameless music with paid-use licence and approved local storage.
Play **each suggested change** and stop for wrong notes or files leaving the group.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a realistic loss of track income.
S1.quote: Learning an AI part checker early may save time, but it cannot make a client order a cello recording.
fieldNote: Her **new AI learning** requires paid lead instruction and commercially permitted, private source music she owns.
She **plays every edit** and stops for errors or storage leakage.

steps.text: Compare ten track invoices and request three months of paid trio dates
Learn checker after paid lead lesson on owned nameless music with paid-use licence/local storage
Play suggested changes; stop wrong notes or storage leakage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the trio manager which practice-track orders the new software will replace. I would still ask for written live fees before reserving a weekend.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tracks bring about one fifth of my own pay, so fewer orders would sting despite our savings. A nine-month reserve buys time; it does not turn lost work into income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll compare my last ten track invoices with new orders and request three months of paid trio dates. In the first year I'll learn the group's new AI part checker only after a paid lesson with the lead, using my own nameless music under a licence allowing paid use and approved local storage; I'll play every suggested change and stop for a wrong note or a file leaving the group.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the track fees. Learning an AI part checker early may save time, but it cannot make a client order a cello recording.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you buy the checker yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, the group's licence and paid lesson must cover the trial. If I have to pay personally, I'll keep the paper part.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you test with a pupil's recording?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would never upload a pupil's playing to test a checker. My own nameless part is enough to hear whether the change works.

say: I'd warn that **2028 thinking AGI** reaches tracks before 2031 playing robots.
I'd ask for **written paid dates** while weddings remain booked.
think: I expect **track orders** to end, costing one fifth of my pay.
Live **wedding cuts** are possible, not my forecast.
do: Count **track income** and request signed paid wedding dates now.
Seek **posted reception work** after 2028 only if live dates fall, schooling/experience qualify, written net after travel replaces losses and journey works.
Keep **trio calls and pupils** until a suitable written offer is signed; request an actual pension statement before stopping work.
feel: I feel **anxious** about expected track loss with time to search.
S2.quote: Nine months saved cannot stand in for years of income.
fieldNote: Expected **2028 track loss** is distinct from conditional live-date cuts.
A job move requires **posted qualification**, replacement net pay after travel, workable journey and signed offer.

steps.text: Seek secondary/counter-experience-qualified posted reception job if live dates fall; written replacement net after travel, journey works
Keep paid trio calls and pupils until suitable signed offer; request actual pension statement before stopping
Total track income and request signed paid wedding dates now

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the trio that thinking AGI by 2028 could make cello practice tracks cheaply. Playing robots follow around 2031, three years later, and paid players need written dates now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the track orders to end in 2028, taking one fifth of my pay. Live wedding sets might also fall later, but I won't call that certain when the diary has bookings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll total track income and ask for signed paid wedding dates. In the first year after 2028, if live bookings also fall, I'll seek a posted music-centre reception job only if my secondary schooling and counter experience qualify, written net pay after travel replaces lost fees and the journey works; I'll keep trio calls and assisted pupils until a suitable offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the expected track loss, though our reserve and nearby employers give me time. I would be alarmed by a collapse in live dates, but that is an extra condition.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you retire at 60 instead of applying?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would get an actual pension statement before deciding to stop at 60. Nine months saved cannot stand in for years of income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is a centre job available now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No centre has offered me a reception job. I would read a real posting and its requirements before putting that pay into our budget.

say: I'd price a **beginner cello circle** before inviting anyone.
I'd require a **signed room agreement** before announcing the class.
think: Tracks may lose value **before 2031** as ordinary software improves.
A **paid senior lead** must cover teaching beyond my beginner skill.
do: Offer **first-steps circle** after signed room/insurance terms and six fees covering hire, paid lead, my teaching/preparation and travel.
Inspect **six loan cellos**; defer and refund everyone if enrollment or instrument safety fails.
Renew **after 2031** only with the same paid floor, room terms and safe cellos; keep booked trio calls.
feel: I feel **anxious** until real fees cover both musicians.
S3.quote: My reserve lets me plan, but a first-steps cello class should earn its own way.
fieldNote: Her **junior skill** limits her to basic hold and open strings under a paid senior lead.
The **six-person floor** covers room, insurance, lead, her preparation/teaching and travel; failure triggers full refund.

steps.text: Offer class after signed room/insurance and six fees cover room, paid lead, own preparation/teaching and travel
Inspect six loan cellos; defer and refund whole group if enrollment or safety fails
Renew after 2031 only with same paid floor, room terms and safe cellos
Keep booked paid trio calls while testing the class

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the town hall that five years until AGI by 2031 gives us time to price a beginner cello circle properly. Playing robots arrive around 2034; I would announce no class before a room agreement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ordinary software might cut practice tracks before 2031. I can show beginners how to hold the cello, but our senior player must be paid to teach harder material and check my plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next spring I'll offer a separate four-week first-steps circle only after the hall signs room and insurance terms, and six adults prepay enough for hire, a paid senior lead, my teaching, preparation and travel. The hall technician must clear six loan cellos before enrollment; if fewer pay or a cello fails, I'll defer and refund everyone. In the first year after 2031 I'll repeat only while those same paid, room and safe-instrument conditions hold, and I'll keep booked trio work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious until the six fees clear and both musicians are paid. My reserve lets me plan, but a first-steps cello class should earn its own way.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if one loan cello is unsafe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I won't count a damaged loan cello as a place. If the technician cannot clear it and a learner cannot bring a sound cello, I'll refund the whole group rather than teach five for an uncovered room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who teaches the harder material?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The lead player would take the hard bowing and supervise my first demonstrations. I would teach only the basic hold and open strings that I can show well.

say: I'd check **actual retirement numbers** during the ten years before 2036.
I'd say **2039 cello robots** do not settle our bills.
think: At **68**, I may still need paid trio and beginner work.
Our **nine-month reserve** does not prove retirement is affordable.
do: Request **actual pension statements** and a written two-year paid-call plan this year.
Keep **paid trio sets** after 2036 while booked; slow only if pension figures and paid work cover bills.
Run **first-steps circle** only with six fees paying room/lead/own teaching/preparation/travel, signed room and safe cellos; otherwise defer/refund everyone.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about distant pay despite secure current work.
S4.quote: I won't declare retirement from a calendar date.
fieldNote: Her **retirement decision** waits for actual pension figures, household bills and paid bookings rather than her birthday.
The **class renewal** keeps the paid floor, written room and safe-instrument gates.

steps.text: Request actual pension statements and written two-year paid-call plan

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my grown children that ten years to AGI by 2036 is enough time to check our retirement numbers. Cello-playing robots follow around 2039, and a birthday doesn't pay the flat charges.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 68 I might still enjoy paid trio calls and first-steps teaching. We have nine months saved, but I don't know whether an actual pension will cover our regular expenses.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll request our pension statements and ask the trio for a written two-year paid-call plan. In the first year after 2036 I'll keep paid sets while booked and run the separate circle only with six fees covering room, paid lead, my preparation, teaching and travel, a signed room agreement and safe cellos; I'll reduce work only if actual pension figures and paid bookings cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distant pay mix, though today's weddings and savings are sound. I won't declare retirement from a calendar date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the class does not meet its floor?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If there are no six deposits or a cello fails inspection, I will defer and refund the group. I won't use our savings to pay the senior player.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Do you know your pension amount now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I haven't received a pension statement yet. I will use the actual figure, not what a friend says people usually get.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because practice-track pay may disappear before I can replace it. Signed wedding dates, an actual pension statement and a real qualifying paid job with written net pay after travel would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Please ask who gets paid for the first hour of a beginner class. A room full of learners is not a wage until the lead and I are paid.

headlineQuote: A room full of learners is not a wage until the lead and I are paid.
portrait: Uma is a **58-year-old junior cellist** with secondary schooling, a partner and grown children.
Her **higher musician pay** and nine-month reserve come with plenty of nearby groups, but every fee needs a booking.
She uses **AI daily** for dates and learns a new part checker only through paid, private and manually checked trials.
She tests a **first-steps class** only with a paid senior lead, six fees, signed room terms and safe cellos.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove one fifth of her own pay from practice tracks.
whatWouldHelp: **Signed wedding calls**, actual pension figures and posted qualifying work with written replacement net pay would help Uma.
